records.title: feat(bridge): fix(loop): scan-B transport resilience â€” REST-dark tower fallback for the merged-landing cross-scan. Live anatomy (GLM Agent 22, Job 486813, 2026-10-30): same session, same boâ€¦ (bridge-20261030-landing-fetch-tower-fallback-r1)

records.reflection_why: The premise-delivered demotion (#3194) is the repo's structural defense against duplicate-minting dispatches, but its only transport is an unauthenticated REST endpoint whose shared-IP budget makes it chronically dark on the documented external-agent runtime â€” so the defense silently evaporates exactly when agent concurrency (and rate pressure) is highest. I witnessed the flip live inside one session and burned a cycle on it. The board query already carries the repo-blessed cure (tower fallback); extending the same proven pattern to scan B closes the defect class at the root instead of asking every future agent to hand-re-verify premise-delivered rows.
records.alternatives_rejected: - (1) In-gates WO title scan (my archived r1 design, docs/bridge/bridge-20261030-premise-delivered-residual-r1.md): withheld â€” it widens #3194's merged-only signal policy, a verdict-plane decision, not mine. (3) Retry-with-backoff on REST: same 60 req/h IP budget â€” retries deepen the 403 storm and still leave the scan dark; a second transport is the only durable cure. (4) Demote-on-failure caching across pick runs: turns a transient dark plane into a sticky blind spot in the BLOCKING direction â€” violates the fail-open contract. (5) Move scan B wholly to the tower: drops body-citations the REST window carries; REST first + tower second preserves the stronger window when available.

records.title: feat(bridge): fix(bridge): full-board drainage join in the landing watchdog (#2516 remedy item 2) - run_verdicts() silently dropped open rows outside the bridge:queued/rejected label pair, so seâ€¦ (bridge-20261030-watchdog-fullboard-join-r1)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: #2516 proved the watchdog's git-join census was structurally blind outside the bridge:queued/rejected label pair: a landed row carrying any other label never surfaced, and the label-plane never-touched fingerprint (updatedAt==createdAt) under-counted the backlog for drainage planning (label-plane 14 vs authoritative git-join 34, material at 2.4x). Root cause: the label filter was allowed to shrink the REPORT surface, though the guard's own reconciliation model names the history plane as ground truth for a landing. The fix makes the join run against ALL open rows and lets the label shape only the message (label_plane tag), never visibility - so future stragglers surface within one cycle instead of accumulating between manual matrix-scoped sweeps.
records.alternatives_rejected: - (1) Admin batch-close and route-B tower reconciler - #2516 remedy items 1/3 are admin/tower-owner lanes, unreachable from the zero-credential public-repo contract. (2) Flagging non-landed non-queued rows as LANDING_AT_RISK - rejected: they may be plain tracker issues; that adds a brand-new false-positive class on the strict surface (the rejected-plane doctrine exists for exactly this reason). (3) Repairing only the never-touched fingerprint (e.g. joining tower claim comments) - symptom patch: the label-plane count would still structurally drift from git-join. (4) A separate new census script - duplicates planes the guard already owns instead of repairing the one SSOT consumers already read.

records.title: feat(bridge): fix(agents): root-cause fix - _cli_resolve parsed the --model flag but never forwarded it to resolve_agent_identity(), so EVERY CLI identity registration ran the model=None -â€¦ (bridge-20261030-agent-identity-cli-model-forward)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: why: The bug is a CLI-adapter-layer defect: the argparse surface advertises --model (help text even documents it) but _cli_resolve dropped it on the floor, so the advertised flag was a silent no-op and every CLI agent landed in the 'unknown-' model namespace. That namespace drives CAS branch claims (agent/{model}-{role}-N) and heartbeat observability, so a dropped flag is not cosmetic - it misnames agents permanently (persistent identity.json). Root-cause layer is the adapter: fix is forwarding the parsed value, plus tests that pin the adapter->implementation contract so the flag-drop class cannot silently recur (any future parser/impl drift breaks the suite).
records.alternatives_rejected: - alternatives_rejected: (1) fix only via AGENT_MODEL env documentation - rejected: keeps the advertised CLI flag broken and pushes the trap onto every operator; (2) re-derive a new agent_name when persisted identity's model prefix mismatches the resolved model - rejected for this slice: renames break heartbeat/cooldown continuity and CAS branch mapping; recorded here as a known limitation, needs its own cohesive WO if owners want namespace migration; (3) patch all _cli_* helpers defensively - rejected: audited each; only _cli_resolve drops the flag (_cli_heartbeat forwards model=args.model correctly), speculative edits elsewhere violate smallest-safe-change (P7).
